Learning
AWS can feel overwhelming — dozens of services, complex networking, security concepts, and production best practices that are rarely explained together. entry.title: Rust in Linux: Fixing the Edges, Not the Core
entry.summary: In 2022, Linus Torvalds made the decision to merge Rust support into the Linux kernel - Version 6.1 was the first release to include the new Rust infrastructure. This was not a rejection of C, nor an attempt to rewrite the kernel. C remains the kernel’s foundation. What changed was a recognition that the kernel’s security risks were not coming primarily from its core, but from the vast and expanding perimeter code written by humans under real-world constraints. As the kernel has grown, developers have had to track memory allocations and deallocations manually across complex, asynchronous, and hardware-driven paths — a task that is error-prone even for highly experienced programmers. entry.title: Am I becoming selectively text blind?
entry.summary: Today I was reading a post and when I registered the text turned into an advertisement my brain didn't register the words anymore and I just scrolled down. I think it is the equivalent of tuning out the advertisement banners and images you see on most websites. The problem I see with it is that the advertisement text is woven in with text that is informational. So I'm losing what could be a part of the reasoning or a crucial piece of information. I have seen the same pattern with YouTube creators who review items, and mix the item review with the advertisement. I gotten into the habit of skipping that item entirely. In a video it bothers me not as much but in text it feels like reading a story and getting interrupted by information that is so out of context it doesn't feel good anymore to read the rest. Am I the problem or do you have the same or a similar experience? I understand people make posts for different reasons and it is not my place to ban things, nor do I want to. I'm wondering how other people react when they have the same realization I had.
